bullets.title: Catching the Big Fish: Meditation, Consciousness, and Creativity
bullets.creator: David Lynch
bullets.note: fourhourmail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuohorkk0/d9feh0hpg2qqx/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9kYXZpZF9seW5jaA==)). Filmmaker David Lynch describes his personal methods of capturing and working with ideas and the immense creative benefits he has experienced from the practice of meditation. This book has been recommended to me by many high-calibre creatives, [including drummer Dave Elitch](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuohorkk0/76t7h8hn7x00g/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE4LzExLzI2L2RhdmUtZWxpdGNoLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj01YmY=).

bullets.section: New mic I’m using while traveling —
bullets.title: Shure MV88 iOS Digital Stereo Condenser Microphone
bullets.note: This mic can literally fit inside my closed hand. It plugs right into my iPhone lightning port for easy recording of podcast intros and so on. I use the Shure MOTIV app for audio capture, but the hardware is app agnostic. To get it to my laptop, I use the “Share” feature and AirDrop. Here’s the official description: “The MV88 iOS digital stereo condenser microphone offers content creators unrivaled convenience and professional-quality audio on the go. Simply plug it into your iPhone, iPad, or iPod and hit record in your favorite audio or video recording app to get life-like stereo recordings. Or, personalize your sound with enhanced control over stereo width, polar patterns, EQ, and more with the free ShurePlus™ MOTIV™ app, which features recording, editing, and the option to share your recordings with the world.”

bullets.title: Claudio Naranjo
bullets.note: (born November 24, 1932) is a Chilean-born psychiatrist of Arabic/Moorish, Spanish, and Jewish descent who is considered a pioneer in integrated psychotherapy.

bullets.title: “No person would give up even an inch of their estate, and the slightest dispute with a neighbor can mean hell to pay; yet we easily let others encroach on our lives—worse, we often pave the way for those who will take it over. No person hands out their money to passersby, but to how many do each of us hand out our lives! We’re tight-fisted with property and money, yet think too little of wasting time, the one thing about which we should all be the toughest misers.” — Seneca the Younger \Found in [_The Daily Stoic, which is now only $1.99 in ebook until 1/6.
